context_needed: Population comes only from the title and the notes on the next page (PDF p. 45): 'Sample: noneligible households', i.e. households in BRAC treatment and control villages that were not eligible for the ultra-poor programme; the coefficient is the DiD indirect treatment effect (ITE) on the treatment-village x 4-year-wave interaction. Panel B lets the effect vary by wealth class (near-poor, middle, upper) among non-eligibles. Monetary values are 2007 PPP US$. The direct effects on eligible ultra-poor women are in other tables (e.g. Table III) and must not be mixed with these rows.

rule: When the title or notes say the sample is non-eligible households, every effect in the table is a spillover: put that population in subgroup_or_population ('non-eligible households in treatment villages'), never the programme's target group, so these rows are not read as the main effect. Wealth-class rows stay spillovers, with the class added to the population.
